name: Xerxes
role: King of Persia in the book of Esther
whenBasis: The reign as the rulers' data dates it, from sources outside the Bible. Identification of Esther's Ahasuerus with Xerxes is the majority view; the Septuagint calls him Artaxerxes.
summary: The king who reigned over 127 provinces from India to Cush, called Ahasuerus in Hebrew. In his third year he deposed Queen Vashti for refusing to come to his banquet; in his seventh Esther became queen. He let Haman issue a decree to destroy the Jews, then, reminded on a sleepless night that Mordecai had saved his life, had Haman hanged and gave Mordecai his signet ring and the right to let the Jews defend themselves.
body: Esther shows a king ruled by his advisers and his temper: a decree against every disobedient wife on Memucan's word, the Jews' destruction on Haman's. A law of the Medes and Persians cannot be revoked, so the second decree does not cancel the first; it lets the Jews fight back. The book ends with the tribute he laid on the land and Mordecai second only to him.
Ezra 4:6 records an accusation against Judah and Jerusalem at the start of his reign.

moments.text: The feast in his third year

later.text: Ahasuerus is the Hebrew form of the Persian Xšayāršā, the name the Greeks wrote Xerxes; most scholars identify him with Xerxes I. The Greek Esther calls him Artaxerxes.
Herodotus tells of his invasion of Greece in 480 BC and names his queen Amestris.
